text:
rachel: FYI we're scheduling a low-impact maintenance window this Sunday 02:00-04:00 UTC. Scope: rolling kernel update on edge-router instances, followed by a small canary failover of the routing layer and a short SLO alerting experiment (details below). Purpose: validate fast rollback and make sure the new health-check weighting doesn't regress tail latency.

 tom: Will this touch Dedicated or Reserved pools? any customer-facing downtime?

 rachel: No customer-facing downtime expected. Dedicated pools with reserved capacity will not be drained. We'll run the canary on a non-prod Dedicated pool and a tiny prod edge shard (5% traffic) to validate fallbacks. If anything looks off we'll abort and rollback.

 yara: What is the "SLO alerting experiment" you mentioned?

 rachel: Good question. We're testing a shorter alert aggregation window for p99 to reduce false positives for quick spikes. Current alert: p99 > 4s sustained for 5m. Experiment: temporarily set alert to p99 > 4s sustained for 1m with a higher incident threshold before paging, and collect both metrics. This is for observability only; no service-level target change. If it reduces noisy pages without missing real incidents, we'll propose it as an option.

 tom: Makes sense. How will rollback work if the kernel update causes latency spikes?

 rachel: Rollback Plan: 1) disable canary routing via feature flag; 2) revert edge-router kernel to previous image; 3) re-enable autoscaling warmup and run kv-prefill. Quick commands in runbook.

 rachel: Runbook (shortlink): https://confluence.redwood.ai/maint/edge-kernel-canary-2065. Key rollback snippet (orchestration):

 ```
 infractl feature-flag set edge.canary_routing false --scope=edge-shard-7
 infractl image rollback --service=edge-router --to-image=edge-router:v1.14.3
 infractl autoscaler update --pool=edge-hot --min-ready-check=kv-warm
 ```

 yara: Can we pre-warm model caches and KV before the canary? last time cold KV caused tail spikes.

 rachel: Yes. We'll run a targeted warmup 10m before the canary step. Warmup command:

 ```
 curl -s -X POST https://admin.redwood.internal/kv/warmup \
  -d '{"prefixes":["/models/alpha/","/kv/hot/"],"threads":16,"duration_sec":240}'
 ```

 tom: Please add a silence rule for the noisy latency channel during the window so we don't flood oncall. Also ensure we still page for error-rate or sustained large SLO breaches.

 rachel: Agreed. Plan: silence latency-noise for 02:00-04:30 UTC, keep error-rate and availability pages active. We'll also create a short-lived stricter page (p99 > 6s sustained for 5m) that does page so we're not blind.

 ops-bot: Reminder scheduled: Edge kernel canary start in 24h. Affected services: edge-router, routing-layer. Notifying on-call.

 yara: One more ask: can we tag any long-running eval jobs to be excluded from routing experiments? They caused test pollution last time.

 rachel: Yes, add tag "exclude-from-canary" to job metadata and CC me. We'll ensure scheduler honors that tag during the window.

 tom: I'll run a quick smoketest pre and post canary: 100 concurrent requests to /healthcheck and a sampling of 50 multi-turn model calls. Will post numbers here.

 rachel: Thanks. Ops will publish a TL;DR after the run with p95/p99, error-rate delta, and token-cost delta. Please ack if you reviewed the runbook and have no blockers. :thumbsup:

 tom: ack :thumbsup:

 yara: ack

 rachel: Closing loop: oncall for window is tom (primary), yara (backup). Contact via call if pages spike, otherwise DM first. Will pin runbook in channel.

 sre-bot: Thread pinned to channel by rachel.
